title: Finite-filtration devissage through a triangulated derived functor
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], with bounded-below derived categories and cohomology functors [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. Let $\Phi:D^+(\mathcal A)\to D^+(\mathcal B)$ be an additive triangulated functor, meaning that it is equipped with a natural isomorphism $\Phi(K[1])\cong\Phi(K)[1]$ and carries distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Let $\mathcal S$ be a strictly full subcategory of $\mathcal B$ containing zero and closed under kernels and cokernels of morphisms between its objects and under extensions in $\mathcal B$. Let $r\geq0$, and let $0=F_0\subseteq F_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq F_r=F$ be a finite sequence of subobjects in $\mathcal A$, with quotient objects $Q_i=F_i/F_{i-1}$ for $1\leq i\leq r$. Write $A[0]$ for an object $A$ placed in degree zero. If $H^q(\Phi(Q_i[0]))\in\mathcal S$ for every $i$ and every $q\in\mathbf Z$, then $H^q(\Phi(F[0]))\in\mathcal S$ for every $q\in\mathbf Z$. The inclusions need not be strict; $r=0$ and zero quotients are allowed.

source.place: Tag 0GKY, label lemma-loc-constant-shriek-rel-dim-1, proof final paragraph (finite-filtration reduction); abstract formulation using derived.tex Tag 06UQ, label lemma-cohomology-in-serre-subcategory, and Tag 0152, label lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-cohomology-in-weak-serre-subcategory] with ambient abelian category $\mathcal B$ and weak Serre subcategory $\mathcal S$. Its hypotheses are exactly the assumed strict fullness, containment of zero, kernel and cokernel closure for morphisms between objects of $\mathcal S$, and extension closure. Thus $\mathcal W=\{K\in D^+(\mathcal B):H^q(K)\in\mathcal S\text{ for every }q\in\mathbf Z\}$ is a strictly full triangulated subcategory. By [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory], it contains zero and is closed under taking the middle vertex of a distinguished triangle whose first and third vertices belong to $\mathcal W$.

source.place: Tag 06UQ, label lemma-cohomology-in-serre-subcategory (including bounded versions); Tag 0152, label lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor; applied to the filtration reduction in more-etale.tex Tag 0GKY, label lemma-loc-constant-shriek-rel-dim-1, proof final paragraph.

proof.text: For $0\leq i\leq r$ let $P(i)$ mean $\Phi(F_i[0])\in\mathcal W$, equivalently that all its cohomology objects belong to $\mathcal S$. The base case $P(0)$ holds: $F_0[0]=0$, and additivity of $\Phi$ gives $\mathrm{id}_{\Phi(0)}=\Phi(\mathrm{id}_0)=\Phi(0)=0$. Hence $\Phi(0)$ is a zero object. Its cohomology is zero (compute it on the zero complex using [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]), and $\mathcal S$ contains zero and is closed under isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 06UQ, label lemma-cohomology-in-serre-subcategory (including bounded versions); Tag 0152, label lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor; applied to the filtration reduction in more-etale.tex Tag 0GKY, label lemma-loc-constant-shriek-rel-dim-1, proof final paragraph.

proof.text: For each $1\leq i\leq r$, the subobject inclusion and its quotient give a short exact sequence $0\to F_{i-1}\to F_i\to Q_i\to0$. By [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle] this yields a distinguished triangle $F_{i-1}[0]\to F_i[0]\to Q_i[0]\to F_{i-1}[0][1]$. All three vertices are bounded below, so this is a triangle of $D^+(\mathcal A)$ with its inherited structure [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. Applying the triangulated functor $\Phi$ gives a distinguished triangle $\Phi(F_{i-1}[0])\to\Phi(F_i[0])\to\Phi(Q_i[0])\to\Phi(F_{i-1}[0])[1]$, where the last arrow uses its given shift isomorphism, exactly as in [def-weil-triangulated-category].

source.place: Tag 06UQ, label lemma-cohomology-in-serre-subcategory (including bounded versions); Tag 0152, label lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor; applied to the filtration reduction in more-etale.tex Tag 0GKY, label lemma-loc-constant-shriek-rel-dim-1, proof final paragraph.

proof.text: Assume $1\leq i\leq r$ and $P(i-1)$. The first vertex of the triangle in step 3 belongs to $\mathcal W$ by this induction hypothesis. Its third vertex belongs to $\mathcal W$ by the hypothesis on every $H^q(\Phi(Q_i[0]))$. The middle-vertex closure from step 1, in the sense of [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory], therefore gives $P(i)$. Finite induction gives $P(r)$; since $F_r=F$, this is the desired conclusion for every integer $q$. If $r=0$ the base case already is the conclusion. Equal consecutive subobjects merely give $Q_i=0$, and the same argument applies without any strictness assumption.
